newsitem.title: UK: NWE naphtha ends lower but backwardation widens.
newsitem.headline: NWE naphtha ends lower but backwardation widens.

text.p: NWE naphtha prices ended slightly lower on Thursday but the backwardation in the nearby swaps widened out after Wednesday's cargo deal, traders and brokers said.
June swaps ended down marginally at $181/$182 a tonne and July finished at $177.50/$178.50. The spread traded at $4 and $4.50 before settling at $3.50, they said.

NWE cargo prices were notionally set at $183/$185 cif, down from the $186.75 Egyptian Alex cargo that traded on Wednesday. Offers were heard today at $185 for Dow spec and for an Algerian cargo, with buying interest for pipeline spec material, they said.
"It was very thin...(but) the backwardation moved out a lot today," one broker said.
In the Med, a Spanish trader said most end-users appeared well covered for the rest of June but there was not a great amount of cargoes available either.
"Basically the market is more or less balanced," he said. "It is true there are not many cargoes but there is not a big rush for demand either."
